content.comment_body: Hello, I have a [product_name] in my home electrical setup that manages the lights. I am interested in controlling the [product_name] programmatically (not through the HTML interface), using Java. From what I understand, the [product_name] can take instructions over Ethernet and the S7 protocol. However, I haven't been able to find a suitable API for this purpose. (Libraries like libnodave or Mocha 7 did not work for me...) Does [company_name] offer any official API to manage [product_name] devices? Does the Java S7 Beans Library support [product_name]? Best regards, [user_name]
Hello! I've successfully used Moka with a Java app (on Android) without issues.

[company_name] does not provide an official API for [product_name]. Based on information from other users here, it's unlikely that such an API will be released. Alternatively, you can try this [product_name] API Middleware server: [url] Your [product_name] must be accessible via the internet. You can read data from I1-I4, M1-M4, AI1-AI4, AM1-AM4 and trigger function keys F1-F4. The details in the data and function keys depend on your [product_name] configuration. You can also create a [product_name] Key and use this format to retrieve data: [url]

analysis.insight_summary: Users want to control their [product_name] devices programmatically in Java via the S7 protocol, but find that [company_name] does not provide an official API. They experiment with third-party libraries and middleware, experiencing inconsistent results. The absence of a sanctioned API or clear compatibility info causes uncertainty and pushes users to rely on community-supported or unofficial solutions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [company_name] to offer an official, well-documented Java API for managing [product_name] devices over the S7 protocol and want dependable Java integration. They are also looking for clear information regarding the compatibility of existing libraries with their [product_name] hardware.
